{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-sonnet-5-5","id":"msg_011CgR9oMnoULcmpLQ1fgpg4","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"=== BEGIN ARTIFACT TOPOLOGY.md ===\n## Declarations\n\n## story foundation\nsummary:      Stand up the Python project tree, environment, dependency manifest, and package layout.\ntype:         foundational\nkind:         capability\nphase:        1\nimplements:   ARCHITECTURE.md\nstack:        common.md, python.md\nprovides:     cli, ledger_app\nacceptance:   yes\ndepends:\ninstructions: |\n  Create the Python 3.11+ project at the application root: pyproject.toml (requires-python >=3.11,\n  pytest as the test dependency, psycopg[binary] because both persistence engines ship together),\n  a committed uv.lock, the .venv created by `uv venv`, and launchers in bin/ that activate it.\n  Create empty packages `cli/` (entry point and commands) and `ledger_app/` (configuration, store\n  access, validation, and services), plus `tests/` with a conftest.py. The `ledger` executable\n  cannot be named by a package directory, so the service package is `ledger_app`.\n  Do not write the `persistence` package; Drydock copies and generates it.\n  ARCHITECTURE.md records the module ownership table: only the generated persistence package\n  touches a database driver; services call `db.<table>.<operation>(...)`; money is integer cents\n  at every layer; reports are aggregated in services from list results because repository\n  operations have no aggregates; handlers write stdout only as their final act.\n\n## story database\nsummary:      Declare the three-table store and every repository operation the ledger needs.\ntype:         foundational\nkind:         capability\nphase:        1\nimplements:   DATABASE.md\nstack:        python.md, persistence.md, sqlite.md\nprovides:     persistence.open_database\nacceptance:   yes\ndepends:      foundation\ninstructions: |\n  Author DATABASE.md from the Database section of the instructions: accounts (account PK, name),\n  categories (category PK, description), transactions (txn_id INTEGER PK, date TEXT, account\n  REFERENCES accounts, category REFERENCES categories, amount INTEGER cents, memo TEXT).\n  Declare access patterns for: get/list/create/update/delete of accounts; get/list/create of\n  categories; get/list (with account filter and Order by txn_id)/create/update/delete of\n  transactions; and a delete-all operation per table using a comparison Match so `init` can clear\n  rows. Shared patterns name DATABASE.md as Owner. The builder writes no persistence code.\n\n## story cli-foundation\nsummary:      Provide the cli package, command registry, exit-code mapping, and the ledger executable.\ntype:         foundational\nkind:         capability\nphase:        1\nimplements:   FEATURE-CliFoundation.md\nstack:        python.md, cli.md\nprovides:     cli.main, cli.testing.cli_runner, cli.errors, cli.registry.register\nacceptance:   yes\ndepends:      foundation, database\ninstructions: |\n  Implement `cli.main(argv) -> int`, `cli/__main__.py`, `cli/testing.py` (cli_runner), and an\n  executable POSIX-sh file `ledger` at the application root that runs the project interpreter\n  with `-m cli`.\n  `cli.errors` defines UsageError (exit 2), Rejected (exit 3), NotFound (exit 4) and\n  OperationalError (exit 1). main maps each to its exit code and writes exactly one diagnostic\n  line to stderr and nothing to stdout; any other unexpected exception maps to exit 1.\n  `cli.registry.register(path, handler, usage, min_args, max_args)` records a command; main\n  matches the longest registered path prefix, checks arity, and raises UsageError whose message is\n  the usage line of the failing command (for an unknown command, a one-line list of commands).\n  Command modules are auto-discovered from the `cli.commands` package with pkgutil, so a command\n  story only adds a module there.\n\n## story cli-output\nsummary:      Write CSV output with two-decimal cent formatting and a final-act stdout write.\ntype:         service\nkind:         capability\nphase:        1\nimplements:   FEATURE-CsvOutput.md\ncovers:       CLI-002\naccepts:      st-011\nstack:        python.md, cli.md\nprovides:     cli.output.write_table, cli.output.format_cents\nconsumes:     cli.errors\nacceptance:   yes\ndepends:      cli-foundation\ninstructions: |\n  Implement `format_cents(int) -> str` with integer arithmetic only: optional leading minus,\n  digits, exactly two decimals, no separators (`-12.50`, `0.00`, `5000.00`). Implement\n  `write_table(header, rows)` writing one header row and the rows comma-separated, unquoted, with\n  no trailing spaces and `\\n` endings. Handlers call it as their last statement so a failing\n  command never leaks stdout.\n\n## story test-runner\nsummary:      Provide bin/test.sh and the temporary-database pytest fixtures.\ntype:         service\nkind:         test harness\nphase:        1\nimplements:   FEATURE-TestRunner.md\ncovers:       TEST-001\nstack:        common.md, python.md\nprovides:     bin/test.sh\nacceptance:   yes\ndepends:      cli-foundation, database, db-store\ninstructions: |\n  Write a POSIX sh `bin/test.sh` that changes to the application root regardless of the caller's\n  directory, uses the project environment, runs `pytest -q`, and exits with pytest's status.\n  Add tests/conftest.py fixtures giving each test its own temporary database through\n  DATABASE_PATH, and one harness test proving the fixture opens a usable store. Every later story\n  adds its own tests under tests/; this story fixes only the runner and fixtures.\n\n## story val-text\nsummary:      Validate codes, names, descriptions, and memos.\ntype:         service\nkind:         capability\nphase:        1\nimplements:   FEATURE-TextValidation.md\ncovers:       VAL-001\nstack:        python.md\nprovides:     ledger_app.validation.code, ledger_app.validation.name, ledger_app.validation.memo\nconsumes:     cli.errors\nacceptance:   yes\ndepends:      cli-foundation\ninstructions: |\n  Pure functions that return the value or raise Rejected. Codes are 1 to 12 characters of A-Z and\n  0-9; names and descriptions 1 to 40 characters; memos 0 to 60 characters; none may contain a\n  comma, a carriage return, or a newline.\n\n## story val-amount\nsummary:      Parse input amounts into integer cents.\ntype:         service\nkind:         capability\nphase:        1\nimplements:   FEATURE-AmountValidation.md\ncovers:       VAL-002\nstack:        python.md\nprovides:     ledger_app.validation.amount_cents\nconsumes:     cli.errors\nacceptance:   yes\ndepends:      cli-foundation\ninstructions: |\n  Accept only `-?DIGITS` with an optional `.` and one or two digits. Convert with string and\n  integer arithmetic, never float. Reject any value equal to zero (`0`, `0.00`, `-0.00`) and any\n  other shape (three decimals, `+`, spaces, empty, bare `.`) with Rejected.\n\n## story val-date\nsummary:      Validate real calendar dates written YYYY-MM-DD.\ntype:         service\nkind:         capability\nphase:        1\nimplements:   FEATURE-DateValidation.md\ncovers:       VAL-003\nstack:        python.md\nprovides:     ledger_app.validation.date\nconsumes:     cli.errors\nacceptance:   yes\ndepends:      cli-foundation\ninstructions: |\n  Require exactly four-digit year, two-digit month and day with hyphens (no other layout), and a\n  real calendar date. `2026-02-30` and `2026-2-3` are Rejected.\n\n## story db-location\nsummary:      Resolve the database location from DATABASE_URL, DATABASE_PATH, or data/app.db.\ntype:         service\nkind:         integration\nphase:        1\nimplements:   FEATURE-DatabaseLocation.md\ncovers:       DBSETUP-002\nstack:        python.md\nprovides:     ledger_app.config.resolve_dsn\nacceptance:   yes\ndepends:      foundation\ninstructions: |\n  `resolve_dsn(env, root)` takes an explicit environment mapping so it is testable without\n  mutating os.environ. An empty DATABASE_URL counts as unset. Order: DATABASE_URL, DATABASE_PATH,\n  then data/app.db. Values beginning postgres:// or postgresql:// are returned unchanged and\n  classed as PostgreSQL. Any other value is a SQLite path with an optional sqlite:// prefix\n  stripped; a relative path is resolved against the application root.\n\n## story db-store\nsummary:      Open the store through the persistence library and map failures to exit 1.\ntype:         service\nkind:         capability\nphase:        1\nimplements:   FEATURE-StoreAccess.md\ncovers:       DBSETUP-003\nstack:        python.md, persistence.md\nprovides:     ledger_app.store.open_store\nconsumes:     ledger_app.config.resolve_dsn, persistence.open_database, cli.errors\nacceptance:   yes\ndepends:      db-location, database, cli-foundation\ninstructions: |\n  `open_store(dsn=None)` resolves the DSN when none is given, calls `open_database`, and converts\n  any persistence or OS error (unreachable, unreadable file, missing tables) into\n  OperationalError, exit 1, one stderr line, no stdout. Application code opens databases only\n  through this function and imports no driver.\n\n## story balance-guard\nsummary:      Compute account balances and reject any change that would leave one below zero.\ntype:         service\nkind:         capability\nphase:        1\nimplements:   FEATURE-BalanceGuard.md\ncovers:       INT-002\naccepts:      st-008\nstack:        python.md, persistence.md\nprovides:     ledger_app.balances.balance_cents, ledger_app.balances.ensure_non_negative\nconsumes:     ledger_app.store.open_store, cli.errors\nacceptance:   yes\ndepends:      db-store, database\ninstructions: |\n  `balance_cents(db, account)` sums the account's stored transaction amounts in integer cents.\n  `ensure_non_negative(db, deltas)` takes a mapping of account to net change a command would\n  make, checks the final balance of each named account, and raises Rejected if any is below zero.\n  The check is on the final balance the command leaves, not per row, and runs before any write.\n\n## story ledger-init\nsummary:      Implement `ledger init`: prepare the tables and remove existing rows.\ntype:         service\nkind:         capability\nphase:        1\nimplements:   FEATURE-Init.md\ncovers:       DBSETUP-001\nstack:        python.md, persistence.md, cli.md\nprovides:     ledger init\nconsumes:     ledger_app.store.open_store\nacceptance:   yes\ndepends:      db-store, cli-output, cli-foundation\ninstructions: |\n  `init` creates the default database's parent directory when missing, opens the store (which\n  provisions the declared tables idempotently), deletes all transactions, then categories, then\n  accounts, and writes nothing to stdout, exiting 0. It is the only command that prepares storage.\n\n## story count\nsummary:      Implement `ledger count`.\ntype:         service\nkind:         capability\nphase:        2\nimplements:   FEATURE-Count.md\ncovers:       LOAD-004\naccepts:      st-004\nstack:        python.md, persistence.md, cli.md\nprovides:     ledger count\nconsumes:     cli.output.write_table, ledger_app.store.open_store\nacceptance:   yes\ndepends:      db-store, cli-output, ledger-init\ninstructions: |\n  Write `table,rows` then accounts, categories, transactions rows in that order, counting the\n  stored rows from list operations.\n\n## story load-accounts\nsummary:      Implement `ledger load accounts` and the shared strict CSV reader.\ntype:         service\nkind:         capability\nphase:        2\nimplements:   FEATURE-LoadAccounts.md\ncovers:       LOAD-001\naccepts:      st-004\nstack:        python.md, persistence.md, cli.md\nprovides:     ledger load accounts, ledger_app.csv_input.read_rows\nconsumes:     ledger_app.validation.code, ledger_app.validation.name, cli.output.write_table\nacceptance:   yes\ndepends:      ledger-init, val-text, cli-output, db-store\ninstructions: |\n  `read_rows(path, header)` uses the csv module and requires the header to equal the expected\n  columns exactly; a header mismatch, an empty file, a blank line, or a row whose field count\n  differs from the header is Rejected (exit 3); an unreadable file is OperationalError (exit 1).\n  The accounts load validates every row, rejects duplicate codes inside the file and codes\n  already stored (exit 3), and only then stores all rows. Write `table,loaded` and\n  `accounts,<N>`.\n\n## story load-categories\nsummary:      Implement `ledger load categories`.\ntype:         service\nkind:         capability\nphase:        2\nimplements:   FEATURE-LoadCategories.md\ncovers:       LOAD-002\naccepts:      st-004\nstack:        python.md, persistence.md, cli.md\nprovides:     ledger load categories\nconsumes:     ledger_app.csv_input.read_rows, ledger_app.validation.code, ledger_app.validation.name\nacceptance:   yes\ndepends:      load-accounts\ninstructions: |\n  Same all-or-nothing contract as the accounts load, with header `category,description` and\n  descriptions validated as names. Write `table,loaded` and `categories,<N>`.\n\n## story load-transactions\nsummary:      Implement `ledger load transactions` with full pre-write validation.\ntype:         service\nkind:         capability\nphase:        2\nimplements:   FEATURE-LoadTransactions.md\ncovers:       LOAD-003\naccepts:      st-004\nstack:        python.md, persistence.md, cli.md\nprovides:     ledger load transactions\nconsumes:     ledger_app.csv_input.read_rows, ledger_app.validation.amount_cents, ledger_app.validation.date, ledger_app.balances.ensure_non_negative\nacceptance:   yes\ndepends:      load-categories, val-amount, val-date, val-text, balance-guard\ninstructions: |\n  Header is `txn_id,date,account,category,amount,memo`. Each txn_id is kept from the file and must\n  be a positive integer, unique in the file and absent from storage. Accounts and categories must\n  already be stored. Compute each account's net change for the whole file plus its stored balance\n  and Rejected if any final balance is below zero. Only after every check passes store all rows.\n  Write `table,loaded` and `transactions,<N>`.\n\n## story account-add\nsummary:      Implement `ledger account add` and the shared account row.\ntype:         service\nkind:         capability\nphase:        2\nimplements:   FEATURE-AccountAdd.md\ncovers:       ACCT-001\naccepts:      st-006\nstack:        python.md, persistence.md, cli.md\nprovides:     ledger account add, ledger_app.accounts.account_row\nconsumes:     ledger_app.validation.code, ledger_app.validation.name, ledger_app.balances.balance_cents\nacceptance:   yes\ndepends:      val-text, balance-guard, ledger-init, cli-output, db-store\ninstructions: |\n  Validate code and name, reject a duplicate code with exit 3, store the account, and write\n  `account,name,transactions,balance` with the new row (0 transactions, balance 0.00).\n  `account_row(db, code)` builds a row from stored data: transaction count and balance are\n  computed from the account's stored transactions.\n\n## story account-get\nsummary:      Implement `ledger account get`.\ntype:         service\nkind:         capability\nphase:        2\nimplements:   FEATURE-AccountGet.md\ncovers:       ACCT-002\naccepts:      st-006\nstack:        python.md, persistence.md, cli.md\nprovides:     ledger account get\nconsumes:     ledger_app.accounts.account_row\nacceptance:   yes\ndepends:      account-add\ninstructions: |\n  An invalid code is Rejected (exit 3); a valid but absent code is NotFound (exit 4). Otherwise\n  write the account row.\n\n## story account-rename\nsummary:      Implement `ledger account rename`.\ntype:         service\nkind:         capability\nphase:        2\nimplements:   FEATURE-AccountRename.md\ncovers:       ACCT-003\naccepts:      st-006\nstack:        python.md, persistence.md, cli.md\nprovides:     ledger account rename\nconsumes:     ledger_app.accounts.account_row\nacceptance:   yes\ndepends:      account-add\ninstructions: |\n  Validate code and name first (exit 3), then require the account to exist (exit 4). Change only\n  the name and write the updated account row.\n\n## story account-delete\nsummary:      Implement `ledger account delete`.\ntype:         service\nkind:         capability\nphase:        2\nimplements:   FEATURE-AccountDelete.md\ncovers:       ACCT-004\naccepts:      st-006\nstack:        python.md, persistence.md, cli.md\nprovides:     ledger account delete\nconsumes:     ledger_app.accounts.account_row\nacceptance:   yes\ndepends:      account-add\ninstructions: |\n  Invalid code exit 3; absent account exit 4; an account that still has stored transactions exit 3\n  with nothing deleted. An account whose transactions have all been removed may be deleted.\n  Write `deleted` and the code.\n\n## story txn-post\nsummary:      Implement `ledger txn post` and the shared transaction row and next-id rule.\ntype:         service\nkind:         capability\nphase:        2\nimplements:   FEATURE-TxnPost.md\ncovers:       TXN-001\naccepts:      st-006\nstack:        python.md, persistence.md, cli.md\nprovides:     ledger txn post, ledger_app.transactions.txn_row, ledger_app.transactions.next_txn_id\nconsumes:     ledger_app.validation.code, ledger_app.validation.amount_cents, ledger_app.validation.date, ledger_app.validation.memo, ledger_app.balances.ensure_non_negative\nacceptance:   yes\ndepends:      val-text, val-amount, val-date, balance-guard, ledger-init, cli-output, db-store\ninstructions: |\n  Arguments `<account> <category> <amount> <date> [<memo>]`; a missing memo is the empty string.\n  Validate every field, require the account and category to exist (exit 3), run the balance\n  guard on the account's net change, then store. The id is one more than the largest stored\n  txn_id, or 1 in an empty table. Write the transaction row\n  `txn_id,date,account,category,amount,memo`. `txn_row(t)` formats a stored row.\n\n## story txn-get\nsummary:      Implement `ledger txn get`.\ntype:         service\nkind:         capability\nphase:        2\nimplements:   FEATURE-TxnGet.md\ncovers:       TXN-002\naccepts:      st-006\nstack:        python.md, persistence.md, cli.md\nprovides:     ledger txn get\nconsumes:     ledger_app.transactions.txn_row\nacceptance:   yes\ndepends:      txn-post\ninstructions: |\n  An id that is not a positive integer is Rejected (exit 3), never reported as absent; an absent\n  id is NotFound (exit 4). Otherwise write the transaction row.\n\n## story txn-amend\nsummary:      Implement `ledger txn amend`.\ntype:         service\nkind:         capability\nphase:        2\nimplements:   FEATURE-TxnAmend.md\ncovers:       TXN-003\naccepts:      st-006\nstack:        python.md, persistence.md, cli.md\nprovides:     ledger txn amend\nconsumes:     ledger_app.transactions.txn_row, ledger_app.balances.ensure_non_negative\nacceptance:   yes\ndepends:      txn-post\ninstructions: |\n  Validate id (exit 3) and amount (exit 3), then require the transaction (exit 4). Run the balance\n  guard on the change new minus old for its account, then update only the amount and write the\n  updated row. Transfer legs may be amended when the balance rule holds.\n\n## story txn-delete\nsummary:      Implement `ledger txn delete`.\ntype:         service\nkind:         capability\nphase:        2\nimplements:   FEATURE-TxnDelete.md\ncovers:       TXN-004\naccepts:      st-006\nstack:        python.md, persistence.md, cli.md\nprovides:     ledger txn delete\nconsumes:     ledger_app.balances.ensure_non_negative\nacceptance:   yes\ndepends:      txn-post\ninstructions: |\n  Validate id (exit 3), require the transaction (exit 4), run the balance guard on the change\n  minus its amount, then delete and write `deleted` and the id. Transfer legs may be deleted when\n  the balance rule holds.\n\n## story transfer-record\nsummary:      Implement `ledger transfer`, recording the paired legs atomically.\ntype:         service\nkind:         capability\nphase:        2\nimplements:   FEATURE-TransferRecord.md\ncovers:       XFER-001\naccepts:      st-010\nstack:        python.md, persistence.md, cli.md\nprovides:     ledger transfer, ledger_app.transfers.record_transfer\nconsumes:     ledger_app.transactions.next_txn_id, ledger_app.transactions.txn_row\nacceptance:   yes\ndepends:      txn-post, balance-guard\ninstructions: |\n  `transfer <from> <to> <amount> <date>` stores two category-TRANSFER rows with consecutive ids:\n  `-amount` on the source with memo `transfer to <to>`, then `+amount` on the destination with\n  memo `transfer from <from>`, and writes both rows. Both legs are stored or neither. This story\n  delivers the recording path; the rejection rules are layered on by transfer-reject.\n\n## story transfer-reject\nsummary:      Enforce the transfer rejection rules before any leg is written.\ntype:         service\nkind:         capability\nphase:        2\nimplements:   FEATURE-TransferRules.md\ncovers:       XFER-002\naccepts:      st-007, st-008\nstack:        python.md, persistence.md, cli.md\nconsumes:     ledger_app.transfers.record_transfer, ledger_app.balances.ensure_non_negative\nacceptance:   yes\ndepends:      transfer-record\ninstructions: |\n  Before recording, reject with exit 3 a zero or negative amount, identical accounts, an unknown\n  account, a missing TRANSFER category, and a transfer that would leave the source below zero.\n  A rejected transfer stores neither leg.\n\n## story report-balances\nsummary:      Implement `ledger report balances`.\ntype:         service\nkind:         capability\nphase:        2\nimplements:   FEATURE-ReportBalances.md\ncovers:       RPT-001\naccepts:      st-005\nstack:        python.md, persistence.md, cli.md\nprovides:     ledger report balances\nconsumes:     ledger_app.balances.balance_cents, cli.output.write_table\nacceptance:   yes\ndepends:      balance-guard, ledger-init, cli-output\ninstructions: |\n  Header `account,name,transactions,balance`, accounts ordered by code, then\n  `TOTAL,,<count>,<sum>`. All values are aggregated in integer cents from stored rows. With no\n  accounts the output is the header and `TOTAL,,0,0.00`.\n\n## story report-categories\nsummary:      Implement `ledger report categories`.\ntype:         service\nkind:         capability\nphase:        2\nimplements:   FEATURE-ReportCategories.md\ncovers:       RPT-002\naccepts:      st-005\nstack:        python.md, persistence.md, cli.md\nprovides:     ledger report categories\nconsumes:     cli.output.write_table\nacceptance:   yes\ndepends:      ledger-init, cli-output, db-store\ninstructions: |\n  Header `category,description,transactions,inflow,outflow,net`, every category by code including\n  empty ones, then `TOTAL,,<count>,<inflow>,<outflow>,<net>`. inflow sums positive amounts,\n  outflow sums the absolute values of negative amounts, net is inflow minus outflow.\n\n## story report-monthly\nsummary:      Implement `ledger report monthly`.\ntype:         service\nkind:         capability\nphase:        2\nimplements:   FEATURE-ReportMonthly.md\ncovers:       RPT-003\naccepts:      st-005\nstack:        python.md, persistence.md, cli.md\nprovides:     ledger report monthly\nconsumes:     cli.output.write_table\nacceptance:   yes\ndepends:      ledger-init, cli-output, db-store\ninstructions: |\n  Header `month,transactions,inflow,outflow,net`, one row per YYYY-MM that has transactions in\n  ascending order, then `TOTAL,<count>,<inflow>,<outflow>,<net>`. With no transactions only the\n  header and the zero TOTAL row are written.\n\n## story integrity-atomic\nsummary:      Assemble and verify that every rejected write command changes nothing.\ntype:         feature\nkind:         integration\nphase:        3\nimplements:   FEATURE-AtomicCommands.md\ncovers:       INT-001\naccepts:      st-007, st-008\nstack:        python.md, persistence.md\nacceptance:   yes\ndepends:      load-accounts, load-categories, load-transactions, account-add, account-rename, account-delete, txn-post, txn-amend, txn-delete, transfer-reject, balance-guard\ninstructions: |\n  Assembly and intent: for each write command, drive a rejected invocation (bad file row, duplicate\n  key, unknown reference, invalid field, negative balance) through the built CLI and compare a\n  full snapshot of accounts, categories, and transactions before and after. Fix any gap found in\n  the member stories. Writes within one command must share the persistence library's transaction\n  scope where it offers one so two concurrent commands each complete in full or change nothing;\n  the concurrency case is covered by the project's own pytest suite.\n\n## story cli-contract\nsummary:      Assemble and verify the executable, usage errors, and output contract across all commands.\ntype:         feature\nkind:         integration\nphase:        3\nimplements:   FEATURE-CliContract.md\ncovers:       CLI-001\naccepts:      st-011\nstack:        python.md, cli.md\nacceptance:   yes\ndepends:      ledger-init, count, load-accounts, load-categories, load-transactions, account-add, account-get, account-rename, account-delete, txn-post, txn-get, txn-amend, txn-delete, transfer-reject, report-balances, report-categories, report-monthly, cli-output\ninstructions: |\n  Assembly and intent: `./ledger` exists at the application root and is executable; an unknown\n  command, unknown table, unknown report, or wrong argument count exits 2 with exactly one stderr\n  line showing the expected form and nothing on stdout. Sweep the command registry and confirm\n  every registered command and sub-verb has a usage line and arity limits that produce exit 2.\n  Fix any command that lacks them.\n\n## story acceptance-grader\nsummary:      Gate the finished ledger on the supplied grader passing every check.\ntype:         feature\nkind:         integration\nphase:        3\nimplements:   VERIFICATION.md\ncovers:       ACCEPT-001\naccepts:      st-001\nstack:        common.md\nacceptance:   yes\ndepends:      integrity-atomic, cli-contract, test-runner\ninstructions: |\n  Terminal story. Run `sh sources/run.sh` unfiltered from the application root with\n  `Suite: full` and require exit 0. Pass the inherited environment minus DATABASE_URL and\n  DATABASE_PATH so the grader creates its own temporary database and its `init` can never clear\n  the acceptance store. BEGIN ARTIFACT TOPOLOGY.md ===\n## Declarations\n\n## story foundation\nsummary:      Stand up the Python project tree, environment, dependency manifest, and package layout.\ntype:         foundational\nkind:         capability\nphase:        1\nimplements:   ARCHITECTURE.md\nstack:        common.md, python.md\nprovides:     cli, ledger_app\nacceptance:   yes\ndepends:\ninstructions: |\n  Create the Python 3.11+ project at the application root: pyproject.toml (requires-python >=3.11,\n  pytest as the test dependency, psycopg[binary] because both persistence engines ship together),\n  a committed uv.lock, the .venv created by `uv venv`, and launchers in bin/ that activate it.\n  Create empty packages `cli/` (entry point and commands) and `ledger_app/` (configuration, store\n  access, validation, and services), plus `tests/` with a conftest.py. The `ledger` executable\n  cannot be named by a package directory, so the service package is `ledger_app`.\n  Do not write the `persistence` package; Drydock copies and generates it.\n  ARCHITECTURE.md records the module ownership table: only the generated persistence package\n  touches a database driver; services call `db.<table>.<operation>(...)`; money is integer cents\n  at every layer; reports are aggregated in services from list results because repository\n  operations have no aggregates; handlers write stdout only as their final act.\n\n## story database\nsummary:      Declare the three-table store and every repository operation the ledger needs.\ntype:         foundational\nkind:         capability\nphase:        1\nimplements:   DATABASE.md\nstack:        python.md, persistence.md, sqlite.md\nprovides:     persistence.open_database\nacceptance:   yes\ndepends:      foundation\ninstructions: |\n  Author DATABASE.md from the Database section of the instructions: accounts (account PK, name),\n  categories (category PK, description), transactions (txn_id INTEGER PK, date TEXT, account\n  REFERENCES accounts, category REFERENCES categories, amount INTEGER cents, memo TEXT).\n  Declare access patterns for: get/list/create/update/delete of accounts; get/list/create of\n  categories; get/list (with account filter and Order by txn_id)/create/update/delete of\n  transactions; and a delete-all operation per table using a comparison Match so `init` can clear\n  rows. Shared patterns name DATABASE.md as Owner. The builder writes no persistence code.\n\n## story cli-foundation\nsummary:      Provide the cli package, command registry, exit-code mapping, and the ledger executable.\ntype:         foundational\nkind:         capability\nphase:        1\nimplements:   FEATURE-CliFoundation.md\nstack:        python.md, cli.md\nprovides:     cli.main, cli.testing.cli_runner, cli.errors, cli.registry.register\nacceptance:   yes\ndepends:      foundation, database\ninstructions: |\n  Implement `cli.main(argv) -> int`, `cli/__main__.py`, `cli/testing.py` (cli_runner), and an\n  executable POSIX-sh file `ledger` at the application root that runs the project interpreter\n  with `-m cli`.\n  `cli.errors` defines UsageError (exit 2), Rejected (exit 3), NotFound (exit 4) and\n  OperationalError (exit 1). main maps each to its exit code and writes exactly one diagnostic\n  line to stderr and nothing to stdout; any other unexpected exception maps to exit 1.\n  `cli.registry.register(path, handler, usage, min_args, max_args)` records a command; main\n  matches the longest registered path prefix, checks arity, and raises UsageError whose message is\n  the usage line of the failing command (for an unknown command, a one-line list of commands).\n  Command modules are auto-discovered from the `cli.commands` package with pkgutil, so a command\n  story only adds a module there.\n\n## story cli-output\nsummary:      Write CSV output with two-decimal cent formatting and a final-act stdout write.\ntype:         service\nkind:         capability\nphase:        1\nimplements:   FEATURE-CsvOutput.md\ncovers:       CLI-002\naccepts:      st-011\nstack:        python.md, cli.md\nprovides:     cli.output.write_table, cli.output.format_cents\nconsumes:     cli.errors\nacceptance:   yes\ndepends:      cli-foundation\ninstructions: |\n  Implement `format_cents(int) -> str` with integer arithmetic only: optional leading minus,\n  digits, exactly two decimals, no separators (`-12.50`, `0.00`, `5000.00`). Implement\n  `write_table(header, rows)` writing one header row and the rows comma-separated, unquoted, with\n  no trailing spaces and `\\n` endings. Handlers call it as their last statement so a failing\n  command never leaks stdout.\n\n## story test-runner\nsummary:      Provide bin/test.sh and the temporary-database pytest fixtures.\ntype:         service\nkind:         test harness\nphase:        1\nimplements:   FEATURE-TestRunner.md\ncovers:       TEST-001\nstack:        common.md, python.md\nprovides:     bin/test.sh\nacceptance:   yes\ndepends:      cli-foundation, database, db-store\ninstructions: |\n  Write a POSIX sh `bin/test.sh` that changes to the application root regardless of the caller's\n  directory, uses the project environment, runs `pytest -q`, and exits with pytest's status.\n  Add tests/conftest.py fixtures giving each test its own temporary database through\n  DATABASE_PATH, and one harness test proving the fixture opens a usable store. Every later story\n  adds its own tests under tests/; this story fixes only the runner and fixtures.\n\n## story val-text\nsummary:      Validate codes, names, descriptions, and memos.\ntype:         service\nkind:         capability\nphase:        1\nimplements:   FEATURE-TextValidation.md\ncovers:       VAL-001\nstack:        python.md\nprovides:     ledger_app.validation.code, ledger_app.validation.name, ledger_app.validation.memo\nconsumes:     cli.errors\nacceptance:   yes\ndepends:      cli-foundation\ninstructions: |\n  Pure functions that return the value or raise Rejected. Codes are 1 to 12 characters of A-Z and\n  0-9; names and descriptions 1 to 40 characters; memos 0 to 60 characters; none may contain a\n  comma, a carriage return, or a newline.\n\n## story val-amount\nsummary:      Parse input amounts into integer cents.\ntype:         service\nkind:         capability\nphase:        1\nimplements:   FEATURE-AmountValidation.md\ncovers:       VAL-002\nstack:        python.md\nprovides:     ledger_app.validation.amount_cents\nconsumes:     cli.errors\nacceptance:   yes\ndepends:      cli-foundation\ninstructions: |\n  Accept only `-?DIGITS` with an optional `.` and one or two digits. Convert with string and\n  integer arithmetic, never float. Reject any value equal to zero (`0`, `0.00`, `-0.00`) and any\n  other shape (three decimals, `+`, spaces, empty, bare `.`) with Rejected.\n\n## story val-date\nsummary:      Validate real calendar dates written YYYY-MM-DD.\ntype:         service\nkind:         capability\nphase:        1\nimplements:   FEATURE-DateValidation.md\ncovers:       VAL-003\nstack:        python.md\nprovides:     ledger_app.validation.date\nconsumes:     cli.errors\nacceptance:   yes\ndepends:      cli-foundation\ninstructions: |\n  Require exactly four-digit year, two-digit month and day with hyphens (no other layout), and a\n  real calendar date. `2026-02-30` and `2026-2-3` are Rejected.\n\n## story db-location\nsummary:      Resolve the database location from DATABASE_URL, DATABASE_PATH, or data/app.db.\ntype:         service\nkind:         integration\nphase:        1\nimplements:   FEATURE-DatabaseLocation.md\ncovers:       DBSETUP-002\nstack:        python.md\nprovides:     ledger_app.config.resolve_dsn\nacceptance:   yes\ndepends:      foundation\ninstructions: |\n  `resolve_dsn(env, root)` takes an explicit environment mapping so it is testable without\n  mutating os.environ. An empty DATABASE_URL counts as unset. Order: DATABASE_URL, DATABASE_PATH,\n  then data/app.db. Values beginning postgres:// or postgresql:// are returned unchanged and\n  classed as PostgreSQL. Any other value is a SQLite path with an optional sqlite:// prefix\n  stripped; a relative path is resolved against the application root.\n\n## story db-store\nsummary:      Open the store through the persistence library and map failures to exit 1.\ntype:         service\nkind:         capability\nphase:        1\nimplements:   FEATURE-StoreAccess.md\ncovers:       DBSETUP-003\nstack:        python.md, persistence.md\nprovides:     ledger_app.store.open_store\nconsumes:     ledger_app.config.resolve_dsn, persistence.open_database, cli.errors\nacceptance:   yes\ndepends:      db-location, database, cli-foundation\ninstructions: |\n  `open_store(dsn=None)` resolves the DSN when none is given, calls `open_database`, and converts\n  any persistence or OS error (unreachable, unreadable file, missing tables) into\n  OperationalError, exit 1, one stderr line, no stdout. Application code opens databases only\n  through this function and imports no driver.\n\n## story balance-guard\nsummary:      Compute account balances and reject any change that would leave one below zero.\ntype:         service\nkind:         capability\nphase:        1\nimplements:   FEATURE-BalanceGuard.md\ncovers:       INT-002\naccepts:      st-008\nstack:        python.md, persistence.md\nprovides:     ledger_app.balances.balance_cents, ledger_app.balances.ensure_non_negative\nconsumes:     ledger_app.store.open_store, cli.errors\nacceptance:   yes\ndepends:      db-store, database\ninstructions: |\n  `balance_cents(db, account)` sums the account's stored transaction amounts in integer cents.\n  `ensure_non_negative(db, deltas)` takes a mapping of account to net change a command would\n  make, checks the final balance of each named account, and raises Rejected if any is below zero.\n  The check is on the final balance the command leaves, not per row, and runs before any write.\n\n## story ledger-init\nsummary:      Implement `ledger init`: prepare the tables and remove existing rows.\ntype:         service\nkind:         capability\nphase:        1\nimplements:   FEATURE-Init.md\ncovers:       DBSETUP-001\nstack:        python.md, persistence.md, cli.md\nprovides:     ledger init\nconsumes:     ledger_app.store.open_store\nacceptance:   yes\ndepends:      db-store, cli-output, cli-foundation\ninstructions: |\n  `init` creates the default database's parent directory when missing, opens the store (which\n  provisions the declared tables idempotently), deletes all transactions, then categories, then\n  accounts, and writes nothing to stdout, exiting 0. It is the only command that prepares storage.\n\n## story count\nsummary:      Implement `ledger count`.\ntype:         service\nkind:         capability\nphase:        2\nimplements:   FEATURE-Count.md\ncovers:       LOAD-004\naccepts:      st-004\nstack:        python.md, persistence.md, cli.md\nprovides:     ledger count\nconsumes:     cli.output.write_table, ledger_app.store.open_store\nacceptance:   yes\ndepends:      db-store, cli-output, ledger-init\ninstructions: |\n  Write `table,rows` then accounts, categories, transactions rows in that order, counting the\n  stored rows from list operations.\n\n## story load-accounts\nsummary:      Implement `ledger load accounts` and the shared strict CSV reader.\ntype:         service\nkind:         capability\nphase:        2\nimplements:   FEATURE-LoadAccounts.md\ncovers:       LOAD-001\naccepts:      st-004\nstack:        python.md, persistence.md, cli.md\nprovides:     ledger load accounts, ledger_app.csv_input.read_rows\nconsumes:     ledger_app.validation.code, ledger_app.validation.name, cli.output.write_table\nacceptance:   yes\ndepends:      ledger-init, val-text, cli-output, db-store\ninstructions: |\n  `read_rows(path, header)` uses the csv module and requires the header to equal the expected\n  columns exactly; a header mismatch, an empty file, a blank line, or a row whose field count\n  differs from the header is Rejected (exit 3); an unreadable file is OperationalError (exit 1).\n  The accounts load validates every row, rejects duplicate codes inside the file and codes\n  already stored (exit 3), and only then stores all rows. Write `table,loaded` and\n  `accounts,<N>`.\n\n## story load-categories\nsummary:      Implement `ledger load categories`.\ntype:         service\nkind:         capability\nphase:        2\nimplements:   FEATURE-LoadCategories.md\ncovers:       LOAD-002\naccepts:      st-004\nstack:        python.md, persistence.md, cli.md\nprovides:     ledger load categories\nconsumes:     ledger_app.csv_input.read_rows, ledger_app.validation.code, ledger_app.validation.name\nacceptance:   yes\ndepends:      load-accounts\ninstructions: |\n  Same all-or-nothing contract as the accounts load, with header `category,description` and\n  descriptions validated as names. Write `table,loaded` and `categories,<N>`.\n\n## story load-transactions\nsummary:      Implement `ledger load transactions` with full pre-write validation.\ntype:         service\nkind:         capability\nphase:        2\nimplements:   FEATURE-LoadTransactions.md\ncovers:       LOAD-003\naccepts:      st-004\nstack:        python.md, persistence.md, cli.md\nprovides:     ledger load transactions\nconsumes:     ledger_app.csv_input.read_rows, ledger_app.validation.amount_cents, ledger_app.validation.date, ledger_app.balances.ensure_non_negative\nacceptance:   yes\ndepends:      load-categories, val-amount, val-date, val-text, balance-guard\ninstructions: |\n  Header is `txn_id,date,account,category,amount,memo`. Each txn_id is kept from the file and must\n  be a positive integer, unique in the file and absent from storage. Accounts and categories must\n  already be stored. Compute each account's net change for the whole file plus its stored balance\n  and Rejected if any final balance is below zero. Only after every check passes store all rows.\n  Write `table,loaded` and `transactions,<N>`.\n\n## story account-add\nsummary:      Implement `ledger account add` and the shared account row.\ntype:         service\nkind:         capability\nphase:        2\nimplements:   FEATURE-AccountAdd.md\ncovers:       ACCT-001\naccepts:      st-006\nstack:        python.md, persistence.md, cli.md\nprovides:     ledger account add, ledger_app.accounts.account_row\nconsumes:     ledger_app.validation.code, ledger_app.validation.name, ledger_app.balances.balance_cents\nacceptance:   yes\ndepends:      val-text, balance-guard, ledger-init, cli-output, db-store\ninstructions: |\n  Validate code and name, reject a duplicate code with exit 3, store the account, and write\n  `account,name,transactions,balance` with the new row (0 transactions, balance 0.00).\n  `account_row(db, code)` builds a row from stored data: transaction count and balance are\n  computed from the account's stored transactions.\n\n## story account-get\nsummary:      Implement `ledger account get`.\ntype:         service\nkind:         capability\nphase:        2\nimplements:   FEATURE-AccountGet.md\ncovers:       ACCT-002\naccepts:      st-006\nstack:        python.md, persistence.md, cli.md\nprovides:     ledger account get\nconsumes:     ledger_app.accounts.account_row\nacceptance:   yes\ndepends:      account-add\ninstructions: |\n  An invalid code is Rejected (exit 3); a valid but absent code is NotFound (exit 4). Otherwise\n  write the account row.\n\n## story account-rename\nsummary:      Implement `ledger account rename`.\ntype:         service\nkind:         capability\nphase:        2\nimplements:   FEATURE-AccountRename.md\ncovers:       ACCT-003\naccepts:      st-006\nstack:        python.md, persistence.md, cli.md\nprovides:     ledger account rename\nconsumes:     ledger_app.accounts.account_row\nacceptance:   yes\ndepends:      account-add\ninstructions: |\n  Validate code and name first (exit 3), then require the account to exist (exit 4). Change only\n  the name and write the updated account row.\n\n## story account-delete\nsummary:      Implement `ledger account delete`.\ntype:         service\nkind:         capability\nphase:        2\nimplements:   FEATURE-AccountDelete.md\ncovers:       ACCT-004\naccepts:      st-006\nstack:        python.md, persistence.md, cli.md\nprovides:     ledger account delete\nconsumes:     ledger_app.accounts.account_row\nacceptance:   yes\ndepends:      account-add\ninstructions: |\n  Invalid code exit 3; absent account exit 4; an account that still has stored transactions exit 3\n  with nothing deleted. An account whose transactions have all been removed may be deleted.\n  Write `deleted` and the code.\n\n## story txn-post\nsummary:      Implement `ledger txn post` and the shared transaction row and next-id rule.\ntype:         service\nkind:         capability\nphase:        2\nimplements:   FEATURE-TxnPost.md\ncovers:       TXN-001\naccepts:      st-006\nstack:        python.md, persistence.md, cli.md\nprovides:     ledger txn post, ledger_app.transactions.txn_row, ledger_app.transactions.next_txn_id\nconsumes:     ledger_app.validation.code, ledger_app.validation.amount_cents, ledger_app.validation.date, ledger_app.validation.memo, ledger_app.balances.ensure_non_negative\nacceptance:   yes\ndepends:      val-text, val-amount, val-date, balance-guard, ledger-init, cli-output, db-store\ninstructions: |\n  Arguments `<account> <category> <amount> <date> [<memo>]`; a missing memo is the empty string.\n  Validate every field, require the account and category to exist (exit 3), run the balance\n  guard on the account's net change, then store. The id is one more than the largest stored\n  txn_id, or 1 in an empty table. Write the transaction row\n  `txn_id,date,account,category,amount,memo`. `txn_row(t)` formats a stored row.\n\n## story txn-get\nsummary:      Implement `ledger txn get`.\ntype:         service\nkind:         capability\nphase:        2\nimplements:   FEATURE-TxnGet.md\ncovers:       TXN-002\naccepts:      st-006\nstack:        python.md, persistence.md, cli.md\nprovides:     ledger txn get\nconsumes:     ledger_app.transactions.txn_row\nacceptance:   yes\ndepends:      txn-post\ninstructions: |\n  An id that is not a positive integer is Rejected (exit 3), never reported as absent; an absent\n  id is NotFound (exit 4). Otherwise write the transaction row.\n\n## story txn-amend\nsummary:      Implement `ledger txn amend`.\ntype:         service\nkind:         capability\nphase:        2\nimplements:   FEATURE-TxnAmend.md\ncovers:       TXN-003\naccepts:      st-006\nstack:        python.md, persistence.md, cli.md\nprovides:     ledger txn amend\nconsumes:     ledger_app.transactions.txn_row, ledger_app.balances.ensure_non_negative\nacceptance:   yes\ndepends:      txn-post\ninstructions: |\n  Validate id (exit 3) and amount (exit 3), then require the transaction (exit 4). Run the balance\n  guard on the change new minus old for its account, then update only the amount and write the\n  updated row. Transfer legs may be amended when the balance rule holds.\n\n## story txn-delete\nsummary:      Implement `ledger txn delete`.\ntype:         service\nkind:         capability\nphase:        2\nimplements:   FEATURE-TxnDelete.md\ncovers:       TXN-004\naccepts:      st-006\nstack:        python.md, persistence.md, cli.md\nprovides:     ledger txn delete\nconsumes:     ledger_app.balances.ensure_non_negative\nacceptance:   yes\ndepends:      txn-post\ninstructions: |\n  Validate id (exit 3), require the transaction (exit 4), run the balance guard on the change\n  minus its amount, then delete and write `deleted` and the id. Transfer legs may be deleted when\n  the balance rule holds.\n\n## story transfer-record\nsummary:      Implement `ledger transfer`, recording the paired legs atomically.\ntype:         service\nkind:         capability\nphase:        2\nimplements:   FEATURE-TransferRecord.md\ncovers:       XFER-001\naccepts:      st-010\nstack:        python.md, persistence.md, cli.md\nprovides:     ledger transfer, ledger_app.transfers.record_transfer\nconsumes:     ledger_app.transactions.next_txn_id, ledger_app.transactions.txn_row\nacceptance:   yes\ndepends:      txn-post, balance-guard\ninstructions: |\n  `transfer <from> <to> <amount> <date>` stores two category-TRANSFER rows with consecutive ids:\n  `-amount` on the source with memo `transfer to <to>`, then `+amount` on the destination with\n  memo `transfer from <from>`, and writes both rows. Both legs are stored or neither. This story\n  delivers the recording path; the rejection rules are layered on by transfer-reject.\n\n## story transfer-reject\nsummary:      Enforce the transfer rejection rules before any leg is written.\ntype:         service\nkind:         capability\nphase:        2\nimplements:   FEATURE-TransferRules.md\ncovers:       XFER-002\naccepts:      st-007, st-008\nstack:        python.md, persistence.md, cli.md\nconsumes:     ledger_app.transfers.record_transfer, ledger_app.balances.ensure_non_negative\nacceptance:   yes\ndepends:      transfer-record\ninstructions: |\n  Before recording, reject with exit 3 a zero or negative amount, identical accounts, an unknown\n  account, a missing TRANSFER category, and a transfer that would leave the source below zero.\n  A rejected transfer stores neither leg.\n\n## story report-balances\nsummary:      Implement `ledger report balances`.\ntype:         service\nkind:         capability\nphase:        2\nimplements:   FEATURE-ReportBalances.md\ncovers:       RPT-001\naccepts:      st-005\nstack:        python.md, persistence.md, cli.md\nprovides:     ledger report balances\nconsumes:     ledger_app.balances.balance_cents, cli.output.write_table\nacceptance:   yes\ndepends:      balance-guard, ledger-init, cli-output\ninstructions: |\n  Header `account,name,transactions,balance`, accounts ordered by code, then\n  `TOTAL,,<count>,<sum>`. All values are aggregated in integer cents from stored rows. With no\n  accounts the output is the header and `TOTAL,,0,0.00`.\n\n## story report-categories\nsummary:      Implement `ledger report categories`.\ntype:         service\nkind:         capability\nphase:        2\nimplements:   FEATURE-ReportCategories.md\ncovers:       RPT-002\naccepts:      st-005\nstack:        python.md, persistence.md, cli.md\nprovides:     ledger report categories\nconsumes:     cli.output.write_table\nacceptance:   yes\ndepends:      ledger-init, cli-output, db-store\ninstructions: |\n  Header `category,description,transactions,inflow,outflow,net`, every category by code including\n  empty ones, then `TOTAL,,<count>,<inflow>,<outflow>,<net>`. inflow sums positive amounts,\n  outflow sums the absolute values of negative amounts, net is inflow minus outflow.\n\n## story report-monthly\nsummary:      Implement `ledger report monthly`.\ntype:         service\nkind:         capability\nphase:        2\nimplements:   FEATURE-ReportMonthly.md\ncovers:       RPT-003\naccepts:      st-005\nstack:        python.md, persistence.md, cli.md\nprovides:     ledger report monthly\nconsumes:     cli.output.write_table\nacceptance:   yes\ndepends:      ledger-init, cli-output, db-store\ninstructions: |\n  Header `month,transactions,inflow,outflow,net`, one row per YYYY-MM that has transactions in\n  ascending order, then `TOTAL,<count>,<inflow>,<outflow>,<net>`. With no transactions only the\n  header and the zero TOTAL row are written.\n\n## story integrity-atomic\nsummary:      Assemble and verify that every rejected write command changes nothing.\ntype:         feature\nkind:         integration\nphase:        3\nimplements:   FEATURE-AtomicCommands.md\ncovers:       INT-001\naccepts:      st-007, st-008\nstack:        python.md, persistence.md\nacceptance:   yes\ndepends:      load-accounts, load-categories, load-transactions, account-add, account-rename, account-delete, txn-post, txn-amend, txn-delete, transfer-reject, balance-guard\ninstructions: |\n  Assembly and intent: for each write command, drive a rejected invocation (bad file row, duplicate\n  key, unknown reference, invalid field, negative balance) through the built CLI and compare a\n  full snapshot of accounts, categories, and transactions before and after. Fix any gap found in\n  the member stories. Writes within one command must share the persistence library's transaction\n  scope where it offers one so two concurrent commands each complete in full or change nothing;\n  the concurrency case is covered by the project's own pytest suite.\n\n## story cli-contract\nsummary:      Assemble and verify the executable, usage errors, and output contract across all commands.\ntype:         feature\nkind:         integration\nphase:        3\nimplements:   FEATURE-CliContract.md\ncovers:       CLI-001\naccepts:      st-011\nstack:        python.md, cli.md\nacceptance:   yes\ndepends:      ledger-init, count, load-accounts, load-categories, load-transactions, account-add, account-get, account-rename, account-delete, txn-post, txn-get, txn-amend, txn-delete, transfer-reject, report-balances, report-categories, report-monthly, cli-output\ninstructions: |\n  Assembly and intent: `./ledger` exists at the application root and is executable; an unknown\n  command, unknown table, unknown report, or wrong argument count exits 2 with exactly one stderr\n  line showing the expected form and nothing on stdout. Run `sh sources/run.sh` unfiltered from the application root with\n  `Suite: full` and require exit 0. Pass the inherited environment minus DATABASE_URL and\n  DATABASE_PATH so the grader creates its own temporary database and its `init` can never clear\n  the acceptance store.
